Lessons.Title: Features of Graphs
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: interpret horizontal and vertical intercepts, extrema, and increasing, constant, and decreasing intervals on graphs of functions, including contextual meaning of h(0) and h(t)=0. First-party Edulytiks adaptation aligned with Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 4 Lesson 6, https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/4/6/preparation.html and student tasks at https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/4/6/index.html (CC BY 4.0). Source Building On HSF-IF.A.2 and Addressing HSF-IF.B.4; never substitute a generic vertex-only algebra exercise for graphical interpretation.

Independent first-party example: a fictional drone follows a continuous piecewise-linear height function H(t) in metres for 0≤t≤8 seconds. Ordered points (0,0),(2,12),(5,12),(8,0) are connected by straight segments. The graph rises during 0–2 seconds, remains level during 2–5, and falls during 5–8. Maximum height is 12 metres for every t in [2,5]; minimum is zero at t=0,8. Both (0,0),(8,0) are horizontal intercepts, and H(0)=0 is the vertical intercept.

A horizontal intercept is a coordinate where the output equals zero; a vertical intercept is the output when input is zero. Maximum and minimum can occur at several inputs, and in a contextual graph should have units. Do not claim that the graph reveals details between points beyond the stated straight-segment modeling assumption.

Student task: create an original accessible sketch from the four ordered pairs, identify features with exact intervals and units, translate H(2)=H(5) and H(8)=0 into sentences, and critique a classmate who calls the entire rising segment the maximum. Compare a graph of distance from home to a graph of height to expose that the meaning of a zero output depends on context.

Teacher-scored rubric (0–2 each, maximum 8): faithful graph with axes/units, correct intercepts/extrema, correct interval analysis, and meaningful function-notation/context explanations. Actual graph creation and open reasoning are teacher assessed; no invented student activity is automatically credited.

KeyConcepts.Title: Intercepts
KeyConcepts.Definition: Horizontal intercepts have output zero; the vertical intercept has input zero.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Report the coordinates and what they mean in the setting.
KeyConcepts.Example: H(0)=0 gives vertical intercept (0,0); H(8)=0 gives horizontal intercept (8,0).

KeyConcepts.Title: Maximum and minimum
KeyConcepts.Definition: Extrema compare output values across the defined domain, not just one small segment.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Give numerical output and the inputs at which it occurs.
KeyConcepts.Example: Maximum 12 m from t=2 through t=5, minimum 0 m at t=0 and 8.

KeyConcepts.Title: Increasing and decreasing intervals
KeyConcepts.Definition: A function increases if its outputs rise as input increases and decreases if they fall.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Describe intervals and flat portions separately.
KeyConcepts.Example: H increases on (0,2), is constant on [2,5], decreases on (5,8).

WorkedExamples.Title: Determine the maximum plateau
WorkedExamples.Question: Connect (0,0),(2,12),(5,12),(8,0) by straight segments. Find maximum and inputs.
WorkedExamples.Method: Connect a labelled original graph or table to exact values; verify calculations independently.
Steps: Outputs rise from zero to 12 by t=2.
The segment from t=2 to t=5 is horizontal at 12.
Later outputs decrease from 12 to zero.
No output exceeds 12 in the specified continuous piecewise model.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Maximum H(t)=12 m for t from 2 to 5 seconds.
WorkedExamples.Check: Endpoints and every point of the plateau have height12.

WorkedExamples.Title: Interpret all zero values
WorkedExamples.Question: When is H(t)=0, and what does it mean?
WorkedExamples.Method: Connect a labelled original graph or table to exact values; verify calculations independently.
Steps: At t=0 the plotted height is0.
From t=0 to2 the height rises; it is positive between.
On 5–8 it falls to zero exactly at8.
Thus the only zeros are t=0 and t=8.
In the fictional scenario the drone is on ground at these times.

WorkedExamples.Title: Compare average rates over intervals
WorkedExamples.Question: Compare rise over t=0 to2 with descent over t=5 to8.
WorkedExamples.Method: Connect a labelled original graph or table to exact values; verify calculations independently.
Steps: Rise is 12−0=12 m in 2s, giving +6 m/s.
Descent is 0−12=−12 m in 3s, giving −4 m/s.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Rise rate +6 m/s, descent rate −4 m/s.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Assuming an extremum occurs at only one time
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Flat maxima can persist across intervals.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Identify all inputs attaining the extreme.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Confusing horizontal intercept with the maximum
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Horizontal intercept means output zero, not greatest output.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Look for axis crossing versus top of graph.

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Its output is constant over the interval.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Label flat portions constant and explain slope zero.

SummaryPoints: Graph features require coordinates, units and interval context.
The original drone model has a height plateau at 12m from 2s to5s.
Horizontal intercepts are (0,0),(8,0) and vertical intercept (0,0).
Plotting and contextual explanation require teacher review.
